Position Description

Reporting to the Chief Development Officer, the Senior Director of Communications manages all projects that support the communications, public relations, marketing, and branding needs of Planned Parenthood of Michigan and related 501(c)(4), PAC, and SuperPAC entities. This leader will fully embody a commitment to race equity; evidenced in all interactions with PPMI colleagues, external stakeholders and in their supervision of staff.

Essential Functions

· Senior Leadership: Serve as a key member of the Development leadership team, contributing to high-level decision-making and ensuring seamless alignment between communications, advocacy, and organizational priorities. Lead the development of an integrated communications strategy that elevates the organization’s brand and amplifies its impact statewide.
· Team Management: Build, mentor, and inspire a high-performing communications team, fostering an environment of creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning. Cultivate leadership within the team, empowering individuals to take ownership of projects and develop professionally.
· Crisis Communication: Lead crisis communications efforts, crafting rapid response strategies, managing high-pressure situations, and mitigating reputational risks while maintaining transparency and trust.
· Project Management: Manage timelines, budgets, and resources, ensuring projects are completed on schedule and within scope. Demonstrate exceptional ability to meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment, particularly during advocacy campaigns and crisis situations, while maintaining high-quality standards. Leverage project management tools like Asana to set clear expectations, track progress, and promote accountability.
· Content Creation: Oversee the creation of compelling, high-quality content, including press releases, op-eds, speeches, donor communications, case for support, campaign storytelling, talking points, social media, and multimedia assets. Ensure all communications are consistent, culturally competent, and aligned with Planned Parenthood’s brand identity and values.
· Media Relations: Build and maintain strong relationships with journalists, editors, and media outlets. Serve as a spokesperson when needed, proactively pitch stories, and manage media inquiries to ensure accurate, timely, and impactful coverage.
· Impact Measurement & Optimization:
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess the effectiveness of communication initiatives. Regularly analyze data, gather insights, and adapt strategies to enhance reach, engagement, and overall impact. Present results to leadership and stakeholders to inform decision-making.
· Advocacy and Electoral Communications: Oversee communication efforts related to electoral activities, including voter education and mobilization, candidate endorsements, and supporting Planned Parenthood’s related 501(c)(4), PAC, and SuperPAC entities.
· Marketing: Direct the marketing of Planned Parenthood of Michigan’s health and education services, managing vendor relationships and ensuring brand consistency.
· Internal Communications: Strengthen internal communication channels to ensure staff are informed, connected, and aligned with organizational goals. Foster a culture of transparency and engagement by coordinating internal newsletters, meetings, and other means of communication to enhance collaboration and team cohesion.
· Stakeholder Engagement: Cultivate and maintain positive relationships with other PPMI team members, stakeholders, partners, and community leaders to advance Planned Parenthood's mission and move collaborative projects forward.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, and this job description can be amended at any time.

Required

At least 5-8 years of donor communications, media relations, case of support, and campaign storytelling experience.
At least 3-4 years of experience in a leadership and/or supervisory role.
Demonstrated skill in partnering with other functional areas to accomplish objectives; incorporating needs, wants and goals from different business unit perspectives into communication materials and/or reporting information designed to meet the end goal and objective.
Demonstrated commitment to Planned Parenthood’s mission, vision and values
Willingness to work flexible hours depending upon organizational needs and commute to statewide events when necessary.

Facilitate meetings, ensuring that all viewpoints, ideas and problems are addressed.

Marketing & Communications Manager - Adath Israel Congregation, Cincinnati, OH

About Adath Israel Congregation

Adath Israel Congregation is a vibrant Conservative synagogue serving the Greater Cincinnati Jewish community. As Cincinnati’s largest Conservative congregation, we are dedicated to helping our congregants build meaningful connections, engage with their Jewish heritage, and grow spiritually.

We strive to be a welcoming home for individuals and families of all backgrounds by offering dynamic worship, lifelong learning, engaging programming, and opportunities for social justice, advocacy, and community involvement. While honoring our rich history, we are committed to evolving to meet the changing needs of our congregation and creating an inclusive community where every member feels valued, supported, and inspired.

About the Role

Adath Israel Congregation is looking for an outstanding full-time Marketing & Communications Manager. If you are a dynamic, flexible, and incisive professional with a track record of impact at a senior level and strong knowledge of the Jewish community, this may be the role for you.

The Marketing & Communications Manager is responsible for leading the organization’s overall communications efforts. The Manager articulates an ongoing communications strategy for the Synagogue and offers fresh, innovative thinking and strategic marketing and communications plans to improve overall awareness and engagement in our programs. This person is responsible for building out the storytelling platform while creating and marketing content for all synagogue events and educational programs.

This role reports to the Chief Operating Officer and oversees the Communications Department, a team responsible for a wide range of communications in support of the synagogue’s goals and objectives. The Marketing & Communications Manager builds strong collaborative relationships with the clergy, leadership team and colleagues across the organization to understand and address organizational and departmental communication. Using data, they evaluate opportunities to improve our communications strategy to reach various stakeholders and increase participation in our synagogue.

Key Responsibilities / Essential Functions

Develop and maintain clear and consistent messaging, branding and standards of excellence at all levels and across all mediums.
Drive the “look and feel” of all communications, ensuring brand consistency.
Oversee the design of print and digital marketing materials and email marketing.
Direct and supervise Communication Marketing Associates.
Manage recurring communications initiatives including weekly programming emails to congregants, the synagogue’s quarterly newsletter as well as ongoing social media work.
Continue to evolve Adath’s marketing plans and strategies.
Manage condolences emails collaborating with the Senior Rabbi.
Manage development and updates to Adath related websites, evaluating usability and making recommendations to improve layout and function.
Build strong relationships with the Adath team and lay leadership. Manage requests for programming communications plans and materials and provide advice and consultation on specific communication strategies.
Communicate with staff and congregants to collect testimonials and internal and external stories.
Receive, manage and respond to routine media requests. Monitor press and social media.
Review, strengthen and enforce established communications workflows and processes already in place.
Supervise staff and outside vendors relating to website management, e-blasts and other electronic communications and additional print, electronic and social media focused projects.
Establish clear benchmarks and metrics for success, evaluating the institution’s progress and regularly reporting out to leadership, and be responsible for the communications department’s meeting of those goals.
Responsibly manage the communications budget.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree.
6+ years’ experience as a communications professional with a passion for non-profit/mission-based work preferred.
Demonstrated ability to work closely and comfortably with senior level management and various stakeholders to develop and deliver clear, consistent, and creative communications across a broad array of channels (both internal & external) for medium-to-large size organizations.
Familiarity with non-profit environments a plus.
Jewish knowledge a significant plus.
Proficient in Canva, Adobe Suite, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Web Design platforms.
Helpful to have knowledge of BeeFree (RGE Studio), Asana Project Management, Shulcloud, Form building.
FLSA classification (Exempt and not eligible for OT).

This position is responsible for managing Modivcare's external communications function, with functional ownership of media relations, press materials, social media, and evergreen PR content for the corporate brand. Reporting to the Director, Corporate Communications, this role serves as the primary point of contact for media inquiries, proactively builds and maintains relationships with healthcare and business journalists, and executes the full lifecycle of earned media activity — from proactive pitching and press release drafting to reactive response and coverage tracking. This role partners cross-functionally to ensure consistency between external messaging and employee-facing communications and collaborates with marketing communications and government and public affairs on relevant external channel content.

This role...

Manages Modivcare's media relations program, serving as the primary corporate contact for inbound media inquiries and proactively pitching stories, commentary, and executive perspectives to healthcare, business, and trade press.
Develops and maintains relationships with journalists, editors, and reporters covering healthcare services and Medicaid managed care, building a durable network that supports earned media objectives.
Drafts, edits, and distributes press releases, media statements, op-eds, and letters to the editor, ensuring accuracy, message alignment, and adherence to brand voice and legal review requirements.
Owns the corporate library of evergreen PR content — including executive biographies, corporate fact sheets, boilerplate language, and approved talking points — maintaining currency and consistency across all external materials.
Creates corporate social media strategy, developing and executing a content calendar that reflects the company's external communications priorities, brand standards, and audience engagement goals, with support from external agency partners as applicable.
Develops strategy and supporting materials for tradeshows.
Monitors corporate social media channels and the broader media landscape for coverage, sentiment, and emerging narratives relevant to Modivcare, escalating issues through appropriate channels.
Coordinates the development of speaking opportunity materials — including speaker abstracts, presentation support content, and award submissions.
Partners with internal communications to ensure alignment between external messaging and employee-facing communications, particularly during significant announcements, organizational changes, or reputational events.
Collaborates with marketing communications on external channel content that intersects with the corporate website, ensuring that PR-driven content and brand-driven content are consistent and mutually reinforcing.
Collaborates with government and public affairs on external channel content that intersects with key policy priorities and milestones.
Measures and reports on earned media performance, social media engagement, and external channel effectiveness.
Supports crisis and incident response communications by preparing draft external statements, monitoring media activity, and coordinating timely distribution of approved materials.
May lead projects and perform other duties as assigned; occasional business travel may be required.

We are interested in speaking to individuals with the following...

Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field required.
Seven (7) plus years of experience in media relations, public relations, or external communications required.
Experience in a healthcare, healthcare services, or Medicaid managed care environment preferred.
Or equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Proven experience in media relations, public relations, or external communications, with a demonstrated track record of securing earned media coverage and managing journalist relationships in a corporate or agency environment.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to draft clear, accurate, and compelling press materials, statements, and social content across a range of formats and audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams — including proactive media outreach, reactive inquiry response, and content production — with strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through.
Strong understanding of the earned media landscape, including how healthcare and business press operates, what drives coverage, and how to position corporate narratives effectively with relevant media outlets.
Familiarity with social media management practices for corporate channels, including content planning, publishing, community monitoring, and performance measurement.
Proven ability to build and maintain productive working relationships with external stakeholders, including journalists, agency partners, and industry contacts.
Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, regulated environment.
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive information, including pre-announcement materials, crisis-related content, and executive communications.
Working knowledge of the healthcare services industry, including the regulatory and reputational dynamics of Medicaid-funded programs; experience in healthcare or Medicaid managed care preferred.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with content management systems, social media management platforms, and media monitoring tools.
Ability to navigate a complex, matrixed organization and collaborate effectively across functions, including legal, investor relations, human resources, and business unit communications teams.

Summary

Job Summary

The Division of Natural Sciences encourages applications for the Senior Communications Specialist position! This role supports the Division of Natural Sciences (NSCI) in the College of Arts and Sciences to develop, plan, lead, and coordinate strategic communications that highlight research, academic programs, student opportunities, and achievements for an external audience. As a member of the college communications team, this position serves as a critical connector between NSCI, college, and university communications partners to support the reputation, recruitment, and retention priorities of NSCI, especially as they relate to college strategic priorities and campus institutional priorities. This position reports to the assistant dean for communications.

The individual in this role must have a strong communications background and excellent skills in organization and prioritization. To facilitate the required activities, the individual must be knowledgeable of the division and its 14 departments and Public Health program as well as college and campus communication strategies and standard processes. Further, the successful candidate must have a demonstrated ability to independently handle multiple self-directed projects that may, at times, have contending priorities and due dates.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

The College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Colorado Boulder is the intellectual core of the university, conducting research, scholarship, creative work and education in more than 60 fields. Our research generates new knowledge, solving some of the world’s most critical problems!

The college leads nationally in undergraduate and graduate education in the natural sciences, social sciences and arts and humanities, bringing world-class research and scholarship to our students, both in and out of the classroom.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Coordinate and Advance NSCI Communications

Serve as the primary communications liaison for departments and programs to coordinate and advance NSCI communication priorities. Maintain partnerships with communicators in related institutes to coordinate stories and announcements, and to broaden reach.
Serve as the communications expert advising department leadership, faculty and staff on communicating department strengths through compelling storytelling.
Collaborate with department leadership and the college’s director of editorial communications to find opportunities to increase NSCI visibility, media engagement and strategic promotion opportunities.
Advise division and department leadership on defining objectives, messaging, audiences and metrics for diverse communications needs across the division.
Advise departments on connecting communications with broader college priorities, campus institutional priorities and current events for greater amplification.
Collaborate with college communications colleagues to advise departments on integrated marketing and communications strategies, content planning and standard processes across web, social media and other digital communications channels to advance NSCI.
Facilitate external communications including requests for interviews, news releases and media requests for experts in partnership with college and campus communications. Partner with the university’s Strategic Relations and Communications team to prepare faculty and staff for positive engagement with the media.
Identify trends, opportunities and audience insights to inform communications planning and priorities.

Develop, Produce and Lead NSCI Communications

Independently design, develop and implement strategic communications plans in collaboration with department, division and college communications leadership that address a complex array of situations, scopes and assignments.
Produce news articles, web copy, social posts, multimedia and other content for publication across NSCI, college and campus channels.
Provide project development and management to build out the division’s critical communications infrastructure and strengthen the division’s visual identity.
Design products and processes that support departmental communications needs at scale.
Work with internal and external partners to ensure messages reach the intended audiences (media, university leadership, partners and the public).
Develop NSCI communications for distribution through the university email marketing platform.
Identify, lead and contribute to college communications campaigns that originate in NSCI, such as new degrees, program name changes or new program launches.
Create and curate compelling visuals for social media and websites within the college’s Digital Asset Management system.

Other

Regularly analyze and deliver market and audience insights and tracking to NSCI leadership on reach, digital engagement, and communications effectiveness.
Support college communications initiatives and projects as assigned.
Participate in professional development activities.
May supervise student employees supporting communications and content development activities.

What You Should Know

The work schedule for this hybrid position is Monday-Friday, 8-5 p.m., with a minimum of 3 in-person days per week. May require more in-person days as needed.

What We Can Offer

The annual salary for this full-time position is $70,900 - $75,000. Onboarding assistance may be available.

Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

Be Statements

Be creative. Be impactful. Be Boulder.

What We Require

Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communication, public relations, marketing or another relevant field.
3+ years of professional-level experience in journalism, communications, public relations, marketing or related field.
A combination of relevant education, training and/or experience may substitute on a year-for-year basis.

What You Will Need

Demonstrated commitment to promoting diverse and inclusive communications and communities.
Sensitivity to and appreciation of cultural, political and geographical differences with the ability to work effectively with faculty, staff and students from around the world.
Strong organizational, prioritization and time-management skills.
Ability to handle multiple tasks, priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.
Ability to adapt to changing situations and priorities.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a complex organizational environment.

What We Would Like You To Have

5+ years of professional-level experience in journalism, communications, public relations, or marketing.
Experience working in a higher education environment.
Experience writing and developing content related to research, science, or other technical subject matter.
Demonstrated experience developing integrated strategic communications content across multiple platforms and audiences.
Familiarity with email marketing and content management systems.
Familiarity with social media platforms.
Experience using Adobe Creative Suite and/or basic photography and multimedia tools.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and support a customer-focused communications environment

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

A current resume.
A cover letter that specifically tells us how your background and experience align with the requirements, qualifications, and responsibilities of the position.

The Alberta Public Service
works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

The Alberta Human Rights Commission works with Albertans to promote awareness of, and appreciation for, human rights and diversity. Its overall goal is to develop inclusive communities in which all Albertans can participate in the social, economic, and cultural life of the province without discrimination.

Created by the Government of Alberta, the Commission is an independent commission that reports to the Minister of Justice. It has a two-fold mandate: to foster equality and to reduce discrimination. It fulfills this mandate through the resolution and settlement of human rights complaints; an administratively fair human rights tribunal process, and through education programs, policy development, and collaborative initiatives.

Role Responsibilities

Are you ready to shape public understanding of human rights in Alberta? This role offers a unique opportunity to develop and implement communications that promote human rights, inform Albertans, and highlight the vital programs and services of the Alberta Human Rights Commission.

Reporting to the Director, Communication, Education and Engagement (CEE), you will lead and support diverse marketing and communications initiatives. This challenging yet rewarding position requires strategic thinking, creativity, and the ability to translate complex human rights issues into clear, accessible messages for a wide range of audiences.

As Communications Consultant, you will lead content creation, develop comprehensive communication plans, and support both internal and external communications initiatives. You'll collaborate closely with internal subject matter experts and CEE colleagues to ensure effective and timely delivery of key messages across various platforms.

Your responsibilities in this role will include but will not be limited to

Developing and executing comprehensive marketing and communications strategies for internal and external audiences, including media relations, digital content, and brand management.
Leading the development and planning for new communication vehicles like newsletters and other digital communication mediums.

Leading public awareness campaigns and initiatives that increase awareness and understanding of human rights and the Commission.
Conducting research and environmental scans to identify trends and inform strategic communication decisions.
Providing expert communications advice and support, including issues management, strategic planning, and plain language audits and reviews.

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to craft clear, concise, and engaging plain language content.

Proficiency with digital communication tools (e.g., Adobe, Canva, email marketing platforms, social media management tools) and content management systems.
Strong knowledge and understanding of social justice principles, such as equity, root causes, diversity, inclusion, racism, and discrimination.
